about: Place-image style test (Josh, 2026-10-14): linocuts read as stereotyped or dated about half the time, and Josh's hypothesis is that a different art style per city makes exploring less samey and keeps people enjoying the art rather than critiquing a repeated style. Each city's places try that city's approved card style (docs/mexico-version.md), plus an abstract version, on two places, next to the current linocut. Run: COUNTRY=es-mx npm run style-test. Output: style-test/es-mx/index.html (not committed).
rules: Contemporary Mexico: today's clothes and objects, everyday life; no sombreros, cacti, skulls, rebozos or costumes. Lettering: only the place's own sign, word for word; no other words anywhere, no dates, no 'HOY', no neighbourhood or city names, no slogans, no brand names or logos. Keep the main scene in the centre; nothing important near the edges.

ciudad-de-mexico.style: Flat matte gouache illustration with simplified shapes and visible but thin brushstrokes, no thick paint, no impasto. Palette: jacaranda purple, dusty pink, ochre, turquoise, deep green
ciudad-de-mexico.colours: jacaranda purple, dusty pink, ochre, turquoise, deep green

oaxaca.style: Naive folk painting with bright saturated colours, flat perspective and careful small details, inspired by Oaxacan folk art and alebrije patterns. Palette: cochineal red, marigold, indigo and turquoise
oaxaca.colours: cochineal red, marigold, indigo and turquoise

puebla.style: Illustration in the style of a hand-painted Talavera tile panel from Puebla: slightly glossy glaze, visible brush marks, a thin decorative tile border. Palette: cobalt blue and white with touches of yellow, ochre and green
puebla.colours: cobalt blue and white with touches of yellow, ochre and green

guadalajara.style: Mid-century modern travel poster illustration: flat colour shapes, subtle grain, bold simple geometry. Palette: terracotta, teal, mustard and sky blue
guadalajara.colours: terracotta, teal, mustard and sky blue

san-miguel-de-allende.style: Mexican mural painting style: flat fresco look, simplified forms, strong rhythmic composition, matte plaster texture. Palette: terracotta, ochre, rose, slate blue and deep green
san-miguel-de-allende.colours: terracotta, ochre, rose, slate blue and deep green

abstract: Abstract colour-block composition: large flat overlapping shapes and a few confident lines suggest the place and the people in it, without detail; bold and contemporary; use the city's colours
